sentenceSets.sentence: His uncompromising position made settlement impossible, which was either principled or counterproductive depending on what the principle was worth.

answerChoices.reasoning: 'Inflexible' means not able or willing to change, fitting a position that makes settlement impossible; 'inflexible' is very close to 'uncompromising.'
'Unyielding' means not giving way, fitting a position that won't budge; 'unyielding' is virtually synonymous with 'uncompromising.'
'Intransigent' means refusing to compromise, fitting an unyielding position; 'intransigent' is very close to 'uncompromising.'
'Rigid' means stiff and unbending, fitting a position that won't move; however, 'rigid' emphasizes stiffness, while 'uncompromising' emphasizes unwillingness to compromise.
'Obstinate' means stubbornly adhering to a position; while fitting an unyielding stance, it emphasizes stubbornness more than principle.
'Stubborn' means unwilling to change; while fitting an inflexible position, it emphasizes stubbornness rather than principled stance.
'Steadfast' means firmly fixed or committed; while fitting unwavering position, it can have positive connotations, while 'uncompromising' is neutral.
'Resolute' means admirably purposeful; while fitting a firm position, it emphasizes determination positively more than unwillingness to compromise.
'Flexible' means willing to change or adapt; the sentence describes an uncompromising position that made settlement impossible, opposite to flexible.
'Accommodating' means willing to make concessions; the sentence describes an uncompromising position that won't move, opposite to accommodating.
'Malleable' means flexible and able to be changed; the sentence describes an uncompromising position, opposite to malleable.

sentenceSets.sentence: She maintained an uncompromising stance on ethics, refusing bribes even when the opportunity would have advanced her career significantly.

answerChoices.reasoning: 'Inflexible' means rigid and not willing to change, fitting a stance that won't bend on ethics; 'inflexible' is very close to 'uncompromising.'
'Unyielding' means not giving way, fitting refusal to accept bribes despite advantage; 'unyielding' is virtually synonymous with 'uncompromising.'
'Intransigent' means refusing to compromise, fitting an unwavering ethical position; 'intransigent' is very close to 'uncompromising.'
'Unrelenting' means not letting up or yielding, fitting a firm ethical stance; however, 'unrelenting' can suggest harshness, while 'uncompromising' emphasizes unwillingness to give ground.
'Principled' means guided by moral principles; while fitting her ethical stance, the sentence emphasizes unwillingness to compromise, not just having principles.
'Virtuous' means morally excellent; while fitting her refusal to accept bribes, the sentence emphasizes inflexibility rather than virtue.
'Righteous' means morally right; while fitting ethical behavior, the sentence emphasizes unwillingness to compromise rather than righteousness.
'Steadfast' means firmly fixed or committed; while fitting unwavering ethical stance, it can suggest virtue, not just inflexibility.
'Corruptible' means able to be corrupted or bribed; the sentence describes someone with an uncompromising stance refusing bribes, opposite to corruptible.
'Flexible' means willing to change or adapt; the sentence describes an uncompromising ethical stance, opposite to flexible.
'Pragmatic' means practical and willing to adapt; the sentence describes refusing practical advantage to maintain ethics, opposite to pragmatic accommodation.

sentenceSets.sentence: The director's uncompromising vision meant every scene, every word, every detail had to be exactly as he imagined, regardless of time or budget constraints.

answerChoices.reasoning: 'Inflexible' means rigid and not willing to change, fitting a vision that can't be altered; 'inflexible' is very close to 'uncompromising.'
'Unyielding' means not giving way, fitting a vision that won't bend to practical constraints; 'unyielding' is virtually synonymous with 'uncompromising.'
'Intransigent' means refusing to compromise, fitting a vision that won't compromise with practical demands; 'intransigent' is very close to 'uncompromising.'
'Unrelenting' means not giving up or yielding; while fitting the vision that won't bend, 'unrelenting' suggests harsh relentlessness.
'Perfectionist' means demanding perfection; while fitting a director who requires exact details, 'perfectionist' emphasizes pursuit of perfection rather than unwillingness to compromise.
'Rigorous' means thorough and demanding; while fitting high standards, 'rigorous' emphasizes thoroughness rather than inflexibility.
'Meticulous' means paying careful attention to detail; while fitting attention to every detail, 'meticulous' emphasizes care rather than unwillingness to compromise.
'Exacting' means making great demands; while fitting high standards, 'exacting' emphasizes demanding nature rather than inflexibility.
'Flexible' means willing to adapt; the sentence describes a vision that won't change regardless of constraints, opposite to flexible.
'Accommodating' means willing to adjust or concede; the sentence describes a vision that won't bend to time or budget, opposite to accommodating.
'Practical' means realistic and concerned with actual circumstances; the sentence describes a vision that ignores practical time and budget constraints, opposite to practical.
